title: Elders must match the revelations or testify that they are true
setting: Elders met in conference at Hiram, Ohio, on 1–2 November 1831. They voted to publish Joseph Smith’s revelations as the Book of Commandments. Several elders signed a statement that the revelations came by inspiration. Some held back, partly over doubts about the plain language Joseph used. Joseph dictated this revelation during the conference, but the exact day is uncertain. His later history says William McLellin then tried to write a revelation and failed.
summary: The revelation speaks to the assembled elders and says their prayers have been heard. It says fears in their hearts kept them from a blessing they sought. It notes they have watched Joseph Smith’s language and imperfections. It then sets a test: pick the least revelation and let the wisest elder write one like it. If they can, they may say they do not know the revelations are true. If they cannot, they are condemned unless they testify. It closes with a promise that the humble will one day see God by the Spirit.

contextNote.title: A test aimed at doubts about language
contextNote.text: Some elders doubted the revelations because Joseph Smith’s wording seemed plain. Verse 5 names that doubt directly: they knew his language and his imperfections. Verse 6 answers with a test, not an argument. Verse 7 lets them withhold their witness if they can write one “like unto” the least revelation. Verse 8 gives the other result: if they fail, they must “bear record” or stand condemned. Verse 3 had said fears blocked them, which ties the doubt to their own hearts. In this passage, the test measures whether the revelations came “from above,” as verse 9 says, not how polished they are.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 67–70 invites readers to value the revelations and seek their own witness. What do verses 3 and 10 say kept the elders from that witness, and what were they asked to set aside?
reviewNote: Read all 14 verses. Official heading gives Hiram, early November 1831, a conference on publishing the revelations and a discussion of their language. JSP historical introduction read: dictated sometime during the 1–2 November conference; Revelation Book 1 dates it 2 November but the editors are unsure. The McLellin attempt comes from Joseph Smith’s later history (recalled, not from the JSP introduction I read), so it is phrased as his history’s claim. Fact-check 2026-10-12: contextNote now cites verse 3, not verse 10, for fears blocking the elders.
